We have template details. The retro_smarts_template shows a transformation: [CH2;D1;+0:1]=[C;H0;D3;+0:2](-[c:3])-[c:4] >> C-[Si](-C)(-C)-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[Li].O=[C;H0;D3;+0:2](-[c:3])-[c:4]

So forward reaction (canonical) is C-[Si]... + O= C... -> alkene product. In retrosynthesis, we break the alkene into a silyl carbanion and a carbonyl? Actually retro: product is alkene with aromatic substituents; precursors are a silyl group attached to CH2-Li (a silyl carbanion) and a carbonyl (aryl ketone). So applying this template to target should give two precursors: a silyl reagent (maybe Me3Si-CH2Li) and an aryl ketone (aryl-CO-aryl). The target is C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2. That's a stilbene derivative with two anisole rings (para-methoxy phenyl). So the product is a trans? Not specified. The template likely works for any diaryl alkene.

Thus we need to apply template to target to get precursors. Use apply_template tool.
